answerNotes.EGG: A hen's egg has a shell, white, and yolk. Recipes sometimes use only one inner part rather than the whole egg.
answerNotes.NEST: A nest is a place for eggs and young. Many birds build nests, but the materials and locations differ from one species to another.
answerNotes.GRASS: Grass commonly covers lawns and meadows. A pasture is land where animals graze on grass and other low plants.
answerNotes.TREE: Trees have woody trunks and branches. Familiar garden trees may provide fruit, flowers, or shade, sometimes all three.
answerNotes.BRANCH: A branch is a woody limb extending from a tree or shrub. A twig is usually a smaller, thinner piece of that growth.
answerNotes.BIRD: Birds have feathers, beaks, and wings. Not every bird flies, so feathers are a more dependable identifying feature than flight alone.
answerNotes.WING: Wings help birds, many insects, and airplanes fly, but their structures differ. The model-airplane scene uses a fixed surface rather than feathers.
answerNotes.BEAK: Beak and bill are two everyday names for a bird's hard mouthpart. Its shape often reflects how the bird gathers food.
answerNotes.SPRING: Spring is the season between winter and summer. Weather and the exact timing of flowers vary by U.S. region.

answerNotes.POND: A pond is a small body of still water. A creek or brook flows along a channel instead.
answerNotes.WATER: Water is the same liquid whether it is in a drinking glass, a garden hose, or a cooking pot. The container changes the scene, not the substance.
answerNotes.EGG: A hen's egg has a shell, white, and yolk. Recipes sometimes use only one inner part rather than the whole egg.
answerNotes.HOP: Hopping uses a springing jump. In hopscotch, the grid determines which spaces are used for one foot or two.
answerNotes.GREEN: Green describes many growing leaves. It is also a color name in its own right, so read whether the clue asks for a plant or its appearance.
answerNotes.LEG: Leg can name a body part or a furniture support. Read the clue's setting before choosing between those ordinary meanings.
answerNotes.SPRING: Spring is the season between winter and summer. Weather and the exact timing of flowers vary by U.S. region.
answerNotes.NIGHT: Night is the dark part of the daily cycle. Dusk is the fading-light period around the approach of night.
answerNotes.BANK: In a water scene, bank means the ground beside a river or creek. In a money scene, it names a financial business.
